Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2025 included net special-item after-tax charges of $57 million, or $0.07 per share, primarily attributable to PPL's IT transformation and integration-related expenses and adjustments associated with the acquisition of Rhode Island Energy. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2026 included net special-item after-tax charges of $43 million or $0.06 per share, primarily attributable to prior-year impacts associated with an ISO New England transmission return on equity reduction and system integration impacts. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2025 included net special-item after-tax charges of $87 million, or $0.12 per share, primarily attributable to PPL's IT transformation and integration-related expenses and adjustments associated with the acquisition of Rhode Island Energy. Kentucky Regulated Segment PPL's Kentucky Regulated segment primarily consists of the regulated electricity and natural gas operations of Louisville Gas and Electric Company and the regulated electricity operations of Kentucky Utilities Company. Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2026 increased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the second quarter of 2026 were flat compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher income due to higher retail rates effective January 1, 2026, offset by higher operating costs, higher depreciation expense and higher interest expense. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2026 increased by $0.06 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the first six months of 2026 increased by $0.03 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher income due to higher retail rates effective January 1, 2026, and increased returns on capital investments, partially offset by lower sales volumes, higher operating costs, higher depreciation expense and higher interest expense. Pennsylvania Regulated Segment PPL's Pennsylvania Regulated segment consists of the regulated electricity delivery operations of PPL Electric Utilities. Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2026 decreased by $0.02 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the second quarter of 2026 decreased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher depreciation expense and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher transmission revenue from additional capital investments. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2026 decreased by $0.02 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the first six months of 2026 decreased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher operating costs, higher depreciation expense and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher transmission revenue from additional capital investments and higher sales volumes largely due to weather. Rhode Island Regulated Segment PPL's Rhode Island Regulated segment consists of the regulated electricity and natural gas operations of Rhode Island Energy. Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2026 increased by $0.03 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the second quarter of 2026 increased by $0.02 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included lower operating costs and higher rider revenue, partially offset by higher depreciation expense. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2026 decreased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the first six months of 2026 increased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included lower operating costs and higher rider revenue, partially offset by higher depreciation expense and higher interest expense. Corporate and Other PPL's Corporate and Other category primarily includes financing costs incurred at the corporate level, certain non-recoverable costs prior to 2026 resulting from commitments made to the Rhode Island Division of Public Utilities and Carriers and the Rhode Island Attorney General's Office in conjunction with the acquisition of Rhode Island Energy, and certain other unallocated costs. Reported earnings in the second quarter of 2026 increased by $0.03 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the second quarter of 2026 were flat compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher interest expense, offset by factors that were not individually significant. Reported earnings in the first six months of 2026 increased by $0.07 per share compared with a year ago. Earnings from ongoing operations in the first six months of 2026 increased by $0.01 per share compared with a year ago. Factors driving earnings results primarily included higher interest income and lower income taxes, partially offset by higher interest expense. 2026 Earnings Forecast PPL's 2026 earnings from ongoing operations forecast range is $1.90 to $1.98 per share, with a midpoint of $1.94 per share. Earnings from ongoing operations is a non-GAAP measure that could differ from reported earnings due to special items that are, in management's view, non-recurring or otherwise not reflective of the company's ongoing operations. title: Por que atendimento humano virou critério na escolha de uma conta PJ para o negócio?
summary: Confira a importância do atendimento humano em uma conta PJ para garantir o acesso a uma pessoa capaz de encontrar a melhor solução.
body_text: Uma venda aprovada que não aparece no saldo, um acesso bloqueado antes do fechamento ou uma dúvida sobre contestação mudam o peso do atendimento. Nesses momentos, a qualidade da conta PJ aparece no tempo até uma resposta capaz de destravar a operação, com contexto e orientação clara. É por isso que o atendimento humano entra nos critérios de escolha. A automação resolve tarefas previsíveis, enquanto uma pessoa preparada cuida das exceções que mexem com caixa, venda e decisão. Atendimento humano em uma conta PJ é o acesso a uma pessoa capaz de entender o contexto, orientar a decisão e acompanhar a solução. A Stone, o banco para quem empreende, conecta esse cuidado à rotina da conta. A tecnologia dá autonomia no dia a dia. Quando algo sai do roteiro, o empreendedor precisa encontrar alguém que saiba onde olhar e o que fazer. O atendimento aparece quando a operação sai do roteiro Um bom aplicativo deve facilitar Pix, pagamentos, consulta de saldo, controle do cartão e acompanhamento das vendas. Ninguém quer falar com um atendente para executar uma tarefa simples que poderia ser resolvida em poucos toques. Mas a rotina de uma empresa também tem exceções. O pagamento de um fornecedor pode vencer no mesmo dia em que um acesso é bloqueado. A compra de estoque pode depender de um recebimento que ainda não apareceu. Uma contestação pode exigir documentos que o empreendedor nunca precisou enviar. Um bom app resolve o previsível. Uma pessoa preparada resolve a exceção. Para uma pessoa física, um problema bancário já causa transtorno. Para quem empreende, o impacto pode alcançar o balcão, o fornecedor, a equipe e o cliente. A resposta precisa considerar essa cadeia, em vez de tratar cada dúvida como um chamado desconectado do negócio. O Banco Central publica um ranking de reclamações contra instituições financeiras , o que ajuda a tirar a escolha do campo da promessa. O indicador não conta toda a história de uma instituição, mas permite observar se determinados problemas aparecem com frequência e comparar o desempenho ao longo do tempo. O Decreto nº 11.034/2022 também estabelece regras gerais para o Serviço de Atendimento ao Consumidor de empresas reguladas pelo poder público federal. Esse piso protege o consumidor, mas cumprir a regra não mostra sozinho se o suporte entende a rotina de uma pequena empresa. Uma conta PJ pode ter muitos recursos e ainda deixar o dono falando com respostas automáticas quando surge um caso fora do menu. Por isso, a avaliação precisa considerar a experiência de resolução, não apenas a quantidade de canais disponíveis. 5 sinais de que o suporte vai resolver seu problema Como separar um atendimento humano de verdade de um botão que apenas transfere a conversa para outra tela? A diferença aparece no caminho até a pessoa, na qualidade da resposta e no que acontece depois do primeiro contato. Antes de escolher uma conta PJ, observe estes sinais: O caminho até uma pessoa está visível e não exige uma sequência interminável de menus, respostas automáticas e tentativas de adivinhar a categoria do problema? A conversa continua do ponto em que você parou , sem obrigar a repetir CNPJ, protocolo, horário, valor e descrição da ocorrência a cada transferência? A resposta informa o que já foi identificado , o que ainda precisa ser analisado, qual é o próximo passo e quando haverá uma atualização? Quem atende consegue tomar providências ou encaminhar o caso para uma equipe com autonomia, em vez de apenas copiar instruções disponíveis no aplicativo? O contato termina com protocolo, registro da orientação e um caminho claro para acompanhar a demanda até o fechamento? Velocidade sozinha engana. Uma resposta em segundos que apenas repete o menu não resolve o caixa. O tempo até o primeiro contato importa, mas o que conta para a operação é o tempo até uma orientação útil ou até a resolução. O mesmo cuidado vale para o tom. Quem está com uma venda pendente não precisa receber uma aula sobre o sistema financeiro. Precisa entender o que aconteceu em linguagem direta, quais informações deve enviar e qual prazo pode considerar no planejamento. Também faz diferença quando o atendente conhece termos da rotina PJ. Prazo de liquidação, contestação, antecipação , limite de usuário e conciliação não podem virar uma conversa em que o empreendedor precisa explicar o próprio trabalho para quem deveria ajudá-lo. Atendimento humano também não significa depender de uma ligação para tudo. O melhor arranjo combina autonomia digital e acesso a uma pessoa. Você resolve tarefas simples pelo aplicativo e encontra apoio quando o caso exige análise, escolha ou acompanhamento. Como testar o atendimento antes de abrir a conta? A abertura da conta já oferece uma primeira amostra. Observe se os documentos pedidos estão claros, se o andamento pode ser acompanhado e se existe orientação quando uma informação é recusada. Se o processo trava e ninguém explica o motivo, esse comportamento pode reaparecer em outras etapas. Comece pelo canal divulgado pela instituição e faça uma pergunta real, sem compartilhar dados sensíveis. Em vez de perguntar apenas quais produtos estão disponíveis, use uma situação de operação. Por exemplo, pergunte como acompanhar uma venda que não entrou na data esperada ou como agir se um funcionário perder o acesso à conta. Repare se a resposta considera o cenário ou apenas entrega um texto genérico. Um bom retorno informa onde consultar os dados, quais informações serão necessárias e como o atendimento continuará se o primeiro passo não resolver. Os indicadores públicos de atendimento do Consumidor.gov.br ajudam a complementar essa análise. A plataforma permite consultar dados como índice de solução, satisfação do consumidor e prazo médio de resposta das empresas participantes. Esses números ganham mais valor quando são lidos junto com os relatos. Uma queixa isolada pode nascer de um caso fora da curva. Um padrão repetido de falta de retorno, transferências e respostas vagas merece atenção. Avaliações recentes nas lojas de aplicativos também ajudam, desde que sejam lidas com critério. Procure recorrência, data e resposta da empresa. Uma nota geral mistura versões antigas do aplicativo, problemas pontuais e experiências que podem não ter relação com o produto PJ. Outro teste é verificar se a instituição diferencia uma dúvida financeira de uma ocorrência operacional. Uma transferência, uma venda no cartão e um acesso de funcionário exigem análises diferentes. Quando todos os casos caem na mesma fila, a resposta costuma demorar mais e voltar com menos contexto. O melhor suporte entende o dinheiro por trás da dúvida O dono de uma loja pode ter equipe, contador e fornecedores por perto, mas muitas decisões continuam chegando ao balcão dele. Se o dinheiro de uma venda atrasa, é essa pessoa que decide se espera, transfere recursos de outra conta ou muda a compra de estoque. Um atendimento preparado leva esse contexto em conta. Ele não decide pelo empreendedor, mas entrega informação suficiente para que a escolha seja feita com segurança. Isso inclui explicar prazos, separar o que já está confirmado do que ainda depende de análise e evitar promessas que não podem ser cumpridas. Na Conta PJ Stone , você reúne recebimentos, Pix, cartão e ferramentas para cuidar da operação, e ainda conta com atendimento humano em até cinco segundos. Afinal, esse suporte faz diferença quando é preciso entender uma ocorrência, encontrar uma informação ou seguir um caso que não cabe em uma resposta automática. Quando a dúvida envolve uma venda específica, concentrar recebimento e conta reduz o empurra-empurra entre empresas diferentes. O contexto da transação fica mais próximo da movimentação financeira, o que facilita identificar onde está a pendência e qual time deve cuidar dela. Essa integração não elimina imprevistos, mas encurta o caminho para investigar o que aconteceu. Essa diferença vale tempo, evita decisões tomadas no escuro e ajuda a preservar a relação com clientes e fornecedores. Ao comparar contas PJ, coloque tarifas, Pix, cartão, recebimentos e ferramentas de gestão na ponta do lápis. Depois, simule um dia difícil. Tente falar com alguém, apresente uma situação concreta e veja se a resposta ajuda você a agir. Uma conta empresarial acompanha o dinheiro que mantém a operação rodando. O atendimento precisa estar à altura dessa responsabilidade. Quem vive de empreender não precisa de mais um canal aberto. Precisa sair da conversa sabendo o que aconteceu, o que fazer e quando vai receber uma nova posição. Este conteúdo é uma forma de apoiar empreendedores na sua jornada. No entanto, cada estabelecimento é único, e nem todas as dicas aqui podem se aplicar ao seu negócio.

title: Disney Legends in Conversation: Chris Berman
summary: An original ESPN personality, Chris Berman is now a celebrated and influential figure in the world of sports broadcasting.
body_text: Disney Legends in Conversation: Chris Berman Brand August 6, 2026 6 min. read The Disney Legends Award ceremony will mark the final day of D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event presented by Visa® , a one-of-a-kind, multi-day fan experience showcasing the very best in creative storytelling and innovation from across the worlds of Disney. Hosted by Ryan Seacrest , the event will be filled with tributes and unforgettable moments to honor and celebrate the icons behind the magic who have made a lasting impact on Disney. This year, The Walt Disney Company’s highest honor will be presented to 13 individuals — Chris Berman , Jerry Bruckheimer , Susan Egan , Eric Goldberg , Anne Hathaway , Bob Iger , Kim Irvine , Dwayne Johnson , the Jonas Brothers , Lin‑Manuel Miranda , and Alan Tudyk — who for generations have defined Disney across entertainment, storytelling, and experiences. In an exclusive Q&A, Chris Berman —who is being recognized in the Television category—reflects on his contributions to the company and what it means to be named a Disney Legend. How does it feel to be honored as a Disney Legend? The title of Legend is overwhelming. If truth be known, I stand on the shoulders of hundreds — maybe thousands — of ESPNers who believed that an idea once deemed preposterous was instead a stroke of genius. All of us rolled up our sleeves and worked tirelessly at something we truly loved, and the result is one of the greatest success stories in broadcasting history. I am honored to represent all of them. What did the early days of ESPN actually feel like behind the scenes? In some ways, we were the Mercury astronauts with a lot less experience. We believed we could orbit the Earth but were only hoping to land safely after each journey. Most of us were in our 20s and 30s, so it was a grown-up post-collegiate gathering of young people — each one doing the work of two or three while having a blast doing it. From my seat on the SportCenter desk in those early days, we were getting to do 30 minutes of sports news and highlights every night. [News anchor] Walter Cronkite did 30 minutes of the whole world every night! It was great. Did ESPN encourage broadcasters to be entertainers, or did that happen naturally? In no way were we instructed to be entertainers. We were expected to get our facts straight because we were the video version of tomorrow’s newspaper. We were encouraged to be ourselves, which I guess in my case allowed me to have fun delivering the information. Sports fans are smart — they’ll very quickly see if you’re putting style over substance, especially on a nightly basis. How did The Walt Disney Company’s acquisition of ESPN expand its footprint? I can remember February 1996 very clearly. Disney CEO Michael Eisner declared that one of the most important parts of the merger with Cap Cities/ABC was acquiring ESPN, and soon thereafter, he visited us in Bristol, Connecticut, and told us the same thing. If you think about it, it was a perfect marriage. Disney Entertainment appeals to everyone — all ages, no matter what you look like. As Nat King Cole sang, for “kids from 1 to 92.” Sports is the same way. Now, add The Walt Disney Company’s innate ability to distribute all of this worldwide, and like I said, it was a perfect marriage. In 2017, ESPN renamed its NFL broadcast studio “ The Chris Berman–Tom Jackson Studio ” in honor of NFL PrimeTime . What did that rarefied distinction mean to you? Tom and I met for the first time in 1987, and just a few months later, we began a broadcast pairing that lasted 30 years. I believe only Johnny Carson and Ed McMahon were together on TV longer. Our personal friendship remains, to this day, stronger than ever. It means that we, and ESPN, did our NFL shows the right way, as they still do. Maybe a little bit of our pixie dust rubs off on everyone as they set foot in the studio. You’ve covered everything from the Super Bowl and the World Series to Stanley Cup and the U.S. Open. Is there a particular game or moment that sticks with you today? I’ve been lucky to witness so much sports history first-hand, but if I had to choose just one, it would be the night Cal Ripken, Jr., passed the immortal Lou Gehrig’s “unreachable star” record of 2130 consecutive Major League Baseball games played — September 6, 1995. It was a night for baseball — but bigger than that, it was a night for America and the American work ethic. President [Bill] Clinton and Vice President [Al] Gore were there, as was Joe DiMaggio. My broadcast partner Buck Martinez and I were smart enough to be quiet for 23 minutes, as they recognized the moment. In truth, we and everyone in Baltimore that night were too choked up with tears of happiness to say anything! As you think about the future of ESPN , what excites you most? One thing about ESPN that was true in the early days and is still true today is our ability to be innovative and to remain ahead of the curve. Our business has changed astronomically during our almost half century of existence but our willingness to take chances has never wavered. Like sports, not everyone resulted in a touchdown or home run, but our winning percentage is pretty darn good. Maybe one day, to revisit once of my earlier answers, we’ll broadcast live from the moon. Don’t put it past us! About the Disney Legends Program The Disney Legends Awards program is a 39-year tradition of The Walt Disney Company, which began when Fred MacMurray was honored in 1987. Including this year’s honorees, a total of 329 Disney Legends has been named. Past Disney Legends include Tim Allen , Julie Andrews , Angela Bassett , Tony Baxter , Kristen Bell , James Cameron , Jamie Lee Curtis , Miley Cyrus , Marc Davis , Robert Downey Jr. , Harrison Ford , Annette Funicello , Josh Gad , Whoopi Goldberg , Jonathan Groff , Steve Jobs , Elton John , Angela Lansbury , Stan Lee , George Lucas , Steve Martin , Burny Mattinson , Alan Menken , Idina Menzel , Hayley Mills , Fess Parker , Ellen Pompeo , Robin Roberts , the Sherman Brothers , Marty Sklar , Dick Van Dyke , Barbara Walters , Betty White , John Williams , Robin Williams , and Oprah Winfrey . title: Will London Ban Standing Drinks? Soho and West End Pub Rules Explained
summary: London’s famous nightlife districts are at the centre of a growing debate after Westminster Council proposed new licensing guidance that could discourage pubs and bars from allowing customers to drink while standing. body_text: London’s famous nightlife districts are at the centre of a growing debate after Westminster Council proposed new licensing guidance that could discourage pubs and bars from allowing customers to drink while standing. The proposal focuses on managing alcohol consumption, reducing disruption in busy areas, and encouraging more seated drinking spaces. However, hospitality leaders and London’s Mayor have criticised the approach, arguing that it could damage the traditional character of pubs and place further pressure on the city’s nightlife economy. The discussion has raised wider questions about how London balances residents’ concerns, public safety, tourism, and the survival of its hospitality industry. Westminster Council’s Proposed Changes to Pub Licensing Westminster Council, which oversees licensing decisions in areas including Soho and the West End, has published a draft licensing policy for consultation. One of the key recommendations is to discourage what is known as “vertical drinking”, a term used to describe customers drinking while standing rather than sitting at tables. The council’s guidance suggests that venues should provide more seating, encourage table service, and reduce large open bar areas designed for high volumes of standing customers. Officials say the aim is not to stop people enjoying London’s nightlife but to prevent excessive drinking, overcrowding, and problems associated with busy entertainment areas. The policy states that venues should encourage customers to sit, enjoy food, and drink in a more controlled environment rather than creating spaces focused mainly on high-volume alcohol sales. Concerns From Hospitality Industry Experts The proposal has received criticism from some licensing experts who believe standing and socialising are important parts of traditional pub culture. Licensing lawyer Philip Kolvin KC argued that standing drinks are not automatically linked to irresponsible behaviour. He suggested that standing areas allow people to meet new people, move around freely, and enjoy pubs as open social spaces. According to critics, traditional pubs have historically been places where people from different backgrounds can interact casually. They argue that forcing customers into fixed seating arrangements could change the atmosphere that makes pubs unique. Supporters of the hospitality sector say that many successful pubs rely on flexible spaces where customers can choose how they socialise. A busy bar area, they argue, is often part of the identity of a British pub. Mayor of London Challenges Licensing Restrictions The Mayor of London has criticised what he describes as overly restrictive licensing policies affecting the capital’s hospitality industry. A spokesperson for the mayor said that restrictions on venues could harm businesses at a time when many pubs, bars, and restaurants are already facing financial pressures. The mayor’s office highlighted new powers being introduced through devolution changes, which would give the Mayor of London a stronger role in licensing decisions across the capital. These powers could allow the mayor to comment on local licensing policies, influence strategically important decisions, and challenge rules that are considered harmful to London’s growth. The mayor has previously spoken against complaints about nightlife in areas known for entertainment. He has argued that people who choose to live in famous nightlife locations should recognise the character and activity that make those areas attractive. What Is the West End Cumulative Impact Zone? The proposed policy also affects the West End Cumulative Impact Zone, an area where there is already a high concentration of pubs, clubs, restaurants, and entertainment venues. Under the draft guidance, authorities could refuse applications for certain new venues, including pubs, bars, fast-food businesses, and entertainment locations, except in specific circumstances. Cumulative impact policies are designed to manage areas where large numbers of licensed venues may create pressure on local communities. Supporters say these policies help control noise, anti-social behaviour, and overcrowding. However, opponents argue that strict licensing rules can make it harder for new businesses to open and can limit investment in areas that depend heavily on tourism and hospitality. Council Says It Is Not Banning Standing at Pubs Westminster Council has rejected claims that it plans to ban standing in pubs. Councillor Tim Barnes, Westminster City Council’s Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Growth and Planning, said the intention is to help venues manage customers and reduce problems such as crowded pavements and excessive drinking. The council said applications will continue to be considered individually and that businesses will still be able to open and expand if they meet licensing requirements. Officials also pointed out that new venues continue to receive approval in Westminster, suggesting that the policy is intended as guidance rather than a complete restriction on nightlife businesses. Impact on London’s Hospitality Sector The debate highlights a wider challenge facing London’s hospitality industry. Pubs, bars, and restaurants are important parts of the city’s economy, providing employment and attracting millions of visitors every year. Soho and the West End are internationally recognised for their nightlife, theatres, restaurants, and entertainment venues. Business owners fear that additional restrictions could make operating more difficult, particularly as venues continue dealing with rising costs, staffing challenges, and changing customer habits. On the other hand, residents and local groups argue that busy nightlife areas must be managed carefully. They point to concerns about noise, overcrowding, and the impact of late-night venues on people who live nearby. Finding a balance between protecting communities and supporting businesses remains one of London’s biggest urban challenges. The Future of Soho and West End Nightlife The consultation on Westminster Council’s licensing policy is likely to continue attracting debate among politicians, residents, business owners, and hospitality experts. The issue is not simply about whether people can stand while drinking at pubs. It represents a larger conversation about what kind of nightlife London wants in the future. Supporters of stricter controls believe better management can create safer and more welcoming entertainment districts. Critics believe excessive regulation could remove the character and spontaneity that have made Soho and the West End internationally famous. As London receives greater powers over licensing decisions, the relationship between local councils, the mayor’s office, and hospitality businesses will remain closely watched. For now, the future of standing drinks in London pubs remains part of a much bigger debate about culture, community, and the role of nightlife in one of the world’s most famous cities. Source The Independent, published on 6 August 2026. Disclaimer This article is a written summary created for informational purposes. It does not represent the official views of Westminster Council, the Mayor of London, hospitality organisations, or any individuals mentioned. Readers should refer to official council documents and original reporting for the latest updates and policy details.

body_text: View All News Compass Pathways Announces New Employee Inducement Grants Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) August 5, 2026 Download (opens in new window) LONDON & NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS), a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care, announced today that Compass granted equity awards under the Compass Pathways plc 2026 Inducement Plan to fourteen newly hired non-executive employees. The equity awards were granted on August 3, 2026 and consisted of options to purchase an aggregate of 139,355 shares and restricted share units or, in the case of employees in the United Kingdom nominal cost options, covering an aggregate of 66,300 shares. The options have an exercise price per share equal to $11.25, the closing price of the Company’s American Depositary Shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on the grant date, and will vest over a four-year period with 25% vesting on the first anniversary of the date of the grant and the remaining 75% vesting in equal monthly installments over the three-year period thereafter, subject to each employee’s continued employment. The restricted share units and nominal cost options will vest in four equal annual installments, subject to each employee’s continued employment. In accordance with NASDAQ Listing Rule 5635(c)(4), the equity awards were approved by the Compensation and Leadership Development Committee of Compass’s Board of Directors and were made as a material inducement to each employee’s employment. About Compass Pathways We believe mental health patients deserve the possibility of a better future. Compass Pathways plc (Nasdaq: CMPS) is a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care. Our initial focus is developing COMP360 psilocybin, a proprietary, investigational, synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). COMP360 is a potentially first-in-class treatment and has Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), as well as Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the UK for TRD. We are leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD, and building upon that robust foundation, we are executing a late-stage trial evaluating COMP360 for PTSD, another condition with high unmet need. Our goal is to advance treatments that move the field of psychiatry towards treatment options that offer rapid onset and sustained durability with infrequent dosing. Compass is headquartered in London, UK, with a U.S. office in New Jersey. We are driven by our purpose of unlocking pathways to be – opening futures filled with possibility. Together, we are on an ambitious journey toward enabling people living with mental health conditions to find clarity through self-discovery, because every journey needs a Compass. title: How to Send Money from Nigeria to Switzerland
summary: A practical guide to sending money from Nigeria to Switzerland: comparing banks, digital services, exchange rates, and what to get right the first time.
body_text: When a friend told me she was moving to Basel to work at one of the pharmaceutical companies there, her first question wasn't about housing or the weather in winter. It was: "How do I get money from home?" She'd heard stories. Someone waiting three weeks for a SWIFT transfer that arrived short. A cousin who paid fees twice over and still couldn't explain where the money went. She just wanted to know if sending naira to Switzerland was going to be a headache every month. I told her it doesn't have to be. But she needed to know what she was doing before sending the first one. The Nigerian community in Switzerland is smaller than in the UK or the US, but it's growing in ways that matter. There are Nigerians at ETH Zurich and the University of Zurich on research fellowships. There are professionals in Geneva working with the UN, WHO, and the dozens of international bodies headquartered there. There are engineers and scientists at Novartis and Roche in Basel. And every month, families in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, and everywhere else are trying to send financial support across that corridor. The demand is real. The confusion about how to do it well is also very real. Why Switzerland Is a Trickier Corridor Than You'd Expect Switzerland uses the Swiss franc, not the euro. Most people know this in theory, but the implications don't land until you're comparing transfer services and wondering why the rates look different from what you'd get sending to Germany or France. The core issue is that most digital remittance services have optimized their infrastructure around EUR transfers. They hold euros in European bank accounts, settle in the eurozone, and pass those efficiency gains to senders. Switzerland sits outside that system. The CHF has its own settlement network, its own banking compliance stack, and some of the faster pathways that work beautifully for EUR transfers introduce friction when CHF is the destination currency. That friction lands in two places in practice: transfers take longer, and the exchange rate applied at settlement is worse than the headline rate you saw when comparing. You might find a service that moves money to a German bank in six hours but takes two days to a Swiss one. Or you find a rate comparison tool quoting you N1,560 to the franc when the rate applied at the actual point of transfer is N1,620. The spread is where money disappears, not the headline fee. As of mid-July 2026, the naira has been holding relatively stable against major European currencies, settling around N1,557 per euro on the official market after significant recovery from the lows of early 2025. The CBN's decision to hold its Monetary Policy Rate at 26.5% has kept foreign portfolio inflows steady and narrowed the gap between official and parallel rates to levels we haven't seen in years. The Swiss franc tracks the euro closely, which means the NGN/CHF exchange environment right now is more predictable than it has been for a long time. That matters for anyone setting up regular transfers. The Three Main Options Worth Considering Let me walk through the realistic paths here, because people either overcomplicate this or pick the first option they see without comparing properly. Bank-to-bank SWIFT transfers are the instinct for most people, especially for large amounts. You go to your Nigerian bank, fill out the required documentation, provide the beneficiary details, and send the wire. It works. The problem is cost. Nigerian banks charge sending fees. Swiss banks charge receiving fees. And in between, a correspondent bank often takes a cut that nobody discloses upfront. A transfer of N500,000 can lose N25,000 to N40,000 across the chain depending on which banks are involved and which routing path the payment takes. For a one-time transfer, say for tuition fees, a rental deposit, or a large family expense, the wire might still be worth it. The bank record, the familiarity of the process, and the lack of transaction limits have value. For monthly recurring support, that cost structure will hurt over time. International digital transfer services like Wise, Remitly, and WorldRemit are the middle ground. They're faster than banks, generally cheaper, and usable from a mobile phone. My habit is to check two or three platforms side by side before committing to any transfer, because the corridor pricing varies more than people expect. That comparison takes less than five minutes and frequently saves real money. African-focused remittance apps are the third category, and I have skin in the game here so I'll name it plainly. We built Afriex to serve corridors like this one, though I'd genuinely encourage you to compare your options and find what fits your specific amounts and banks. What services built for African senders tend to do better is match the reality of sending from Nigeria: naira as the source currency, mobile-first flows that account for Nigerian bank verification steps, and customer support that understands the specific issues that come up with this corridor. That becomes relevant the first time a transfer is flagged and you need someone who actually speaks that language. What You Need to Have Ready on Both Sides I've watched this catch people by surprise: Swiss banks take compliance seriously, and a transfer that arrives with incomplete beneficiary information or an incorrect IBAN gets held or returned. I've seen this delay transfers by five to seven business days on a corridor where speed matters. Before you initiate any transfer, confirm three things with your recipient: the full IBAN, which is 21 characters for Swiss accounts and starts with CH; the account name exactly as it appears on the bank record; and the bank's BIC/SWIFT code. For larger amounts, ask whether the recipient's bank has incoming transfer notification requirements. Some Swiss cantonal banks flag large international inflows and request documentation of source of funds. If the transfer is going toward something where a paper trail matters later, tuition, rent, medical expenses, keep a screenshot of the confirmation, the rate that was applied, and the transaction reference. Switzerland's banking system is precise, and that precision protects you as much as it creates friction. Reading the Exchange Rate Before You Send NGN/CHF is not a widely tracked pair, so most people end up looking at NGN/EUR as the proxy, which is reasonable given how closely the Swiss franc and euro track each other. As of mid-July 2026, that rate sits around N1,557 per euro on the official market, a significant recovery from the N1,774/€ levels seen in January. The naira has strengthened against the pound too, from lows near N1,950/£ to around N1,841/£ this month. The FX stability story in 2026 is real. Weekly FX turnover in Nigeria's official market hit $2.39 billion in the week ending July 17, a 46% jump week-on-week driven almost entirely by spot transactions. That kind of liquidity is what you want to see when you're planning transfers. It means the rate you get today is more likely to reflect the actual market than it would have been in 2024 when thin liquidity exaggerated rate swings. That said, stability is not permanence. If you're setting up a monthly transfer arrangement, build in a small buffer, around 5% above the amount you need to land, to absorb normal rate movement. In a stable period, that buffer sits unused. In a volatile month, you'll appreciate having it. A Realistic Guide to Comparing Fees The headline fee is not the full cost. Here's how to actually compare services for this corridor. The exchange rate margin is the biggest variable. A service advertising zero transfer fees but applying a 2.5% margin above the mid-market rate will cost you more than a service charging N2,500 flat at the mid-market rate, once your transfer gets above roughly N250,000. For smaller amounts under N200,000, flat fees can add up faster. For larger amounts, percentage-margin services often take more. Running the numbers for your specific amount takes a minute and is usually worth doing. Delivery time has real value too. For urgent payments, paying a premium for same-day or next-business-day delivery is a legitimate calculation, not a luxury. Don't optimize purely for cost and then find yourself explaining to your recipient why money they needed on Tuesday arrived on Friday. Transfer limits are also worth understanding clearly before you set up an account with any service. Some platforms cap individual transactions at amounts that require you to split a larger transfer across multiple transactions, each carrying its own fee structure. If you're sending N1.5 million or more, check per-transaction and per-month limits before you start the account verification process. What the Recipient in Switzerland Needs to Know Swiss banks don't always send real-time push notifications for incoming international transfers. Your recipient may need to log into their account and check, rather than wait for an alert. This is not a problem, just a characteristic of how Swiss banking tends to work. For new arrivals in Switzerland who don't yet have a bank account, PostFinance is often the most accessible option because it serves residents regardless of their banking history in other countries. Neon and Yuh, two Swiss fintech apps, also have faster onboarding for people with a valid Swiss residence permit. For time-sensitive situations where the recipient needs cash and the bank account isn't set up yet, some services offer alternative delivery options. This is less common for Switzerland than for markets in West or East Africa, but it's worth checking with whichever platform you're using. Getting This Right the First Time I'll be honest: the Nigeria-to-Switzerland corridor has a reputation for being complicated, and that reputation isn't entirely wrong. Swiss banking compliance requirements, the CHF sitting outside the eurozone, and the relatively thin digital infrastructure for this specific pair combine to create friction that doesn't exist for more trafficked corridors like Nigeria to the UK or Kenya to Germany. Most of that friction is front-loaded. Getting your recipient's details exactly right, choosing a service that handles CHF competently, and understanding the current rate environment takes real effort the first time. Once you have done it once and the money has arrived cleanly, the second and third transfers are routine. The naira is more stable now than it has been in years. The tools available to Nigerian senders have improved significantly. What remains is for more people to do the comparison properly rather than defaulting to a bank wire that charges them three times over and still takes a week. Whether you're sending monthly support to someone studying in Zurich, covering an emergency expense for a family member in Geneva, or handling business payments into Switzerland, the right setup saves real money every month. That's worth taking the time to figure out properly.

title: Modular Data Center: Containers and Deployment
